provenance.command: git archive 981d25c | tar -x -C <oracle>; add scratch in-package capture test internal/gate/zz_control_capture_test.go; cd <oracle>; GOLDEN_OUT=<out> GOPROXY=off GOFLAGS=-mod=readonly go test -count=1 -run ^TestZZControlCapture$ ./internal/gate/
capture_notes: exchanges go through NewControlPlane(collector.NewStore(time.Hour), scoring.NewEngine(), NewVerdictStore(time.Hour), audit.NewSink(log), audit.NewVault()).Handler() served by httptest.NewServer and called with http.DefaultTransport.RoundTrip, so status, Content-Type, X-Content-Type-Options, Retry-After, Cache-Control and Set-Cookie are the real wire headers (peer 127.0.0.1)
nowFn is fixed at Unix 1800000000; the token key is the 32 ASCII bytes 0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef; no EpochManager, so tokens are minted under epoch e1

records are the audit log records each exchange appended, reduced to event type, actor kind, whether the actor and session pseudonyms are present (vault pseudonyms are random per subject), tenant, route class, verdict, risk score, rules, top signals, action, mode, fail reason and key id
loader keeps only the sha256 of the Go inline JavaScript collector body; the Rust port does not carry that script
session_fresh and collect_no_cookie hold one random hsid; only its shape is meaningful
collect_ok scored a minimal report with the oracle engine; collect_ok_stored and collect_ok_sticky are the stored network signals, label and sticky verdict after it
flood_* use WithControlLimiter(time.Minute, 1, 2) on a fresh plane
verdict_token, verdicts, network_residuals and link_and_audit call the control_collect.go domain methods directly with synthetic inputs and a request from 203.0.113.7:4242
config calls the config.go helpers on zero, negative and set values
provenance.scope: Frozen oracle outputs for differential parity only; never regenerate to hide drift
fixture_edits: verdict_token.bind_key and verdict_token.token_bind of the capture output are stored as verdict_token.client_fingerprint and verdict_token.fingerprint_subnet_binding with unchanged values (Go bindKey and tokenBind outputs for the fixed public test request); the rename keeps the secret scan's generic-api-key keyword rule from matching the fixture's own field names. output_sha256 is of the capture output before this rename.
header_projection was added later from a second capture; its own provenance is inside it.

provenance.command: git archive 981d25c | tar -x -C <oracle>; add scratch in-package capture test internal/gate/zz_gatehdr_capture_test.go; cd <oracle>; GOLDEN_IN=<this fixture before header_projection> GOLDEN_OUT=<out> GOPROXY=off GOFLAGS=-mod=readonly go test -count=1 -run ^TestZZGateHeaderCapture$ ./internal/gate/
capture_notes: seen is what the oracle handler observed: proto_major/proto_minor, handler_header (Go Request.Header as (name, value) pairs, names sorted, values in receive order), header_info (Go headerInfo(r)) and build (Go network.Build over it, JSON-encoded)
header_info.names and build.headerOrder are sorted at capture: Go headerInfo collects names by map iteration, whose order is random per run; cookie_names is Go nil, written as []

exchanges: the 33 golden exchanges rebuilt from each exchange's recorded method, path, request_headers (Header.Set) and request body or request_body_len, sent with http.DefaultTransport.RoundTrip to httptest servers in front of the same three planes as the first capture (keyed main, unkeyed, flood WithControlLimiter(time.Minute, 1, 2)); every status equalled the first capture's
raw_http1: request_line, fields (name, value as written on the wire, ': ' separated, CRLF) and body written byte for byte on a TCP connection to an httptest server
http2: one request over TLS with EnableHTTP2 and the server's own client; only the handler-visible header is meaningful
